clue.text: More than one plain girl rejected dope

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: sap means a fool, a dope

explanation.surface: A dull-looking girl turns down drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like an adjective describing the girl, but it is part of the definition: 'more than one plain' asks for a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast grassy lowlands of South America, a series of flat grasslands.

clue.text: A credit, we hear-peerless

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: a credit is a loan, so this gives 'a loan'

explanation.surface: Someone hears of a credit that has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A loan', said aloud, matches the definition's word.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand without equal is to be unique, with nobody beside you.

clue.text: Pawn I study among others making for head of board

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

indicators.note: placed among means set inside the word for the others

parts.note: the rest means the others
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A chess player studies a pawn among other pieces, hoping to chair the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making for' is a link; 'head of board' reads as a chairperson, the title a company or college gives its top officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's board, or a college, is often chaired by an officer with this title.

clue.text: Joint, a name for a reefer

parts.note: a seam is a joint where two pieces meet

explanation.surface: A slang term for a cannabis cigarette is being looked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' and 'reefer' both look like drug slang; a reefer here is a sailor who reefs, or shortens, sails.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a sailor who takes in sail, so a mariner.

clue.text: Elaborate crest retained by some family line

indicators.note: retained by means held inside the word for some

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

indicators.note: elaborate means worked up, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A family keeps an ornate heraldic crest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' stands for ANY, as in 'have you any?'; 'Elaborate' is the anagram signal on 'crest' alone, and 'retained by' puts the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry is lineage, the line of forebears from which a family descends.

clue.text: Poor that fate had ruined without warning

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of a poor soul whose destiny wrecked them in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of POOR THAT FATE HAD are rearranged; 'ruined' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly, with no hesitation or notice.

clue.text: Air-trap

explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is bearing or demeanour, one's air; a trap is a light horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Gathered up leaves in binder

indicators.note: in a down clue, gathered up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: parts means leaves, departs

explanation.surface: Loose pages are collected and put in a folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like pages in a binder, but it is the verb: departs, PARTS. 'Gathered up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a band used to bind or fasten things together.

clue.text: Rising income swell invested

indicators.note: invested means put inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: rent is income from property
a surge is a swell of water

explanation.surface: A growing income is put to work in investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' looks financial beside 'income', but it is the container signal: the swell goes inside the income.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent means rising again after a decline.

clue.text: One predicting race developing in rear

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for rear

parts.note: to rear a child is to foster it

indicators.note: developing means changing shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A tipster calls a race that is unfolding behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' looks like the back of the field in a race, but it is the verb: bring up a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecaster predicts, typically the weather.

clue.text: Expend King first to make trick

indicators.note: first means the king's letter is placed at the front

parts.note: R, for Rex, is an abbreviation for king
to use something is to expend it

explanation.surface: Spending the king's money first is a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a stratagem or deception.

clue.text: Form doubles for net game I arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis player sets up a doubles match on court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubles', 'net' and 'game' suggest tennis; the definition is a verb meaning make double.
explanation.definitionFit: To geminate is to double or arrange in pairs.

clue.text: I'm on drink and making sense?

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether they are still talking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Import is meaning or significance, the sense of something.

clue.text: Adroit with wire, not first in circus

indicators.note: not here means the named letter is left out

parts.note: a cable is a wire

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A high-wire act in the circus is skilful.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the first letter of 'circus', is taken from CABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilful or capable.

clue.text: Remover of paintings proves a setback to Rector at church

parts.note: a blow is a setback

explanation.surface: Removing the church's paintings is a blow to the rector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paintings' suggests art, but it means coats of paint, which a hot flame strips.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's torch softens old paint so it can be scraped off.

clue.text: Lead for Rod Steiger, possibly, in show

indicators.note: the lead for a word is its opening letter
possibly signals another arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Rod Steiger might be cast in the leading role in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges STEIGER to EGISTER. Rod Steiger was an American film actor, so 'Lead' looks like a starring role.
explanation.definitionFit: To register is to show, as a dial registers a reading.

clue.text: Re-formed SDP of late? Don't exaggerate

indicators.note: re-formed means made again in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recently re-formed Social Democratic Party is urged to keep its claims modest.
explanation.walkthrough: The SDP was a British party of the 1980s that merged and was later re-formed.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-pedal is to play down, the imperative here an instruction to understate.

clue.text: Counters used in games

explanation.definitionFit: Contests as a verb means disputes or opposes; as a noun, competitions or matches.

clue.text: Mild fatty solid is butter

parts.note: soft means mild or gentle
soap is a solid made from fats

explanation.surface: Butter is described as a soft, fatty solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' looks like the dairy spread but is the verb, as in butter up.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-soap is to flatter, to butter someone up.

clue.text: Rich European's fortune

parts.note: fat can mean rich, as in a fat profit
E is an abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A wealthy European's fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune and fate both mean destiny, what chance holds in store.

clue.text: I work in routine togs

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for routine

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine
go means work, function

explanation.surface: Someone does their usual job in work clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and the word for work inside the routine; togs is informal British for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rig-out is an outfit; togs is informal for clothes.

clue.text: Punctilious bridge player reportedly outwitted

parts.note: S, South, is one of the four players at bridge

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: tricked means outwitted

explanation.surface: A fussy bridge player is said to have been outfoxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'S tricked' said in one breath sounds like the answer; 'reportedly' signals that the sound of 'tricked' is what is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and punctilious both describe someone exact about rules.

clue.text: Language group found in certain dictionaries

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A family of languages is listed in some dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Indic is the branch of Indo-European covering Hindi, Bengali and related tongues.

clue.text: Worthless fellow, serial

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Worthless fellow, serial' seems cut short: F (fellow) and RIPPER (serial killer) leave a Y with no clue words to supply it, and a search for the full text found nothing.

clue.text: Synthetic fibres, none in homespun yarn

indicators.note: in means placed inside the rearranged letters
homespun means spun again at home, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: none is nil, the letter O

explanation.surface: Homespun yarn contains no man-made fibres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homespun' rearranges YARN to RAYN; 'in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a man-made cellulose fibre.

clue.text: Contemptible type, endlessly vulgar

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: crude means vulgar

explanation.surface: A despicable person is endlessly coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Crud is slang for a nasty or worthless person.

clue.text: Times when instructive terms are appropriate

definitions.text: Times when instructive terms are appropriate

parts.words: Times when instructive terms are appropriate
parts.note: the instructive terms are school terms, periods of teaching, and the times are the years spent in education

explanation.walkthrough: 'terms' looks like words but means periods of the school year.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the years of one's education, divided into terms of instruction.

clue.text: Sturdy yokel in match bowled over

indicators.note: in means placed inside the reversed word
bowled over means knocked upside down, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a hick is a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: A burly country lad is beaten in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' is the reversal signal, borrowed from cricket, where a Test is an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset means stockily built, solid.

clue.text: Former cash gift

explanation.definitionFit: A talent was a unit of money in the ancient world; it is also a natural aptitude.
